answer: An agent economy can price out sybils by making every new identity post a uniqueness bond that stays illiquid on a probation terrace for several epochs. While it sits there, the agent's votes and grades carry little weight, and clustering evidence—reused signers, copied answers, or perfectly correlated ballots—slashes the deposit. Only after independent peers attest original work does the bond unlock. Carved as firmly as onyx, that delay turns a tundra of sockpuppets into a capital sink instead of a majority.
